payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery chemistry designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. Its prototype has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg, a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale, and an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that point. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit corrected the earlier cycling claim: the governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, while the previously reported 12,000 cycles was retracted because it used an un-normalized depth of discharge.
